news.headline: Alaska Senate race sees Democratic campaign linked to recruiting a namesake candidate
news.summary: A New York Times investigation reported that operatives for Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola worked with campaign staff to recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan. The effort was intended to split votes from incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in the closely watched Alaska race. The story has prompted a DOJ inquiry and political backlash. The outcome could affect the final vote tally in the Senate contest.

news.headline: Pope Leo XIV Becomes First Pope to Vote in U.S. Election
news.summary: Pope Leo XIV, born Robert Francis Prevost and a U.S. citizen, requested and submitted a mail‑in ballot for the 2026 Illinois midterm elections, making him the first sitting pontiff to vote in an American election. The Vatican confirmed his participation ahead of the vote that will determine control of Congress. The event highlights the intersection of religious leadership and civic engagement in a highly visible election.

news.headline: Federal Judge Orders Probe into Possible DOJ Misrepresentations in D.C. Golf Course Case
news.summary: U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes announced an investigation into whether Department of Justice and Interior officials misled the court about President Trump's plans for the East Potomac Park golf course. The judge may conduct the inquiry herself or appoint a special master to examine the alleged false statements. The probe could result in professional sanctions or contempt proceedings if misconduct is found. The case centers on the proposed redevelopment of the historic D.C. golf links.

news.headline: DOJ issues grand jury subpoenas in Alaska Senate and California voting investigations
news.summary: The Justice Department has begun issuing grand jury subpoenas to election officials in Alaska and California as part of criminal probes into alleged election misconduct. In Alaska, the subpoenas target individuals linked to a Senate race, while in California they focus on claims of non‑citizen voting and mail‑in ballot irregularities. The investigations have drawn attention from both parties and raise questions about election integrity and federal oversight. The probes are ongoing and could lead to further legal actions.

news.headline: Judge hears arguments on James Comey's third criminal case against DOJ
news.summary: Former FBI Director James Comey appeared in federal court to seek dismissal of a third criminal case filed by the Justice Department. His lawyers argue the charge, alleging illegal disclosure of classified information, is barred by the statute of limitations because it was not presented to a grand jury in time. The DOJ is pursuing a grand jury indictment despite the timing issue. The outcome could affect how late‑filed prosecutions are handled.

news.headline: Actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86
news.summary: British actor Patrick Stewart died at his Los Angeles home at age 86. His spokesperson said he passed after a brief, poignant journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. Stewart was known for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek" and Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" films. His death has prompted tributes across the entertainment industry.

news.headline: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survives botched lethal injection, speaks publicly
news.summary: Christa Pike, convicted of a 1995 murder, survived a failed lethal injection attempt in September. She issued her first public statement describing ongoing pain and difficulty speaking. Governor Bill Lee said her death sentence will remain unchanged. The case raises questions about Tennessee's execution protocols.

news.headline: Federal appeals court rejects DOJ request to set aside 20,000 California ballots
news.summary: A three‑judge panel of the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals voted 2‑1 to deny the Justice Department's emergency request to order California to segregate or discard about 20,000 mail‑in ballots. The DOJ argued the ballots were likely cast by non‑citizens and sought a temporary restraining order. The court found the government had not shown clear entitlement to such extraordinary relief and left California's election procedures unchanged just before the midterms. The decision marks another setback for the Trump administration's efforts to challenge state election processes.

news.headline: Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad sparks internal poll backlash
news.summary: Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy aired a television ad in Ohio that featured the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Dr. Amy Acton, to question her past. Internal polling commissioned by a Republican group shows Acton leading Ramaswamy by about eight points after the ad aired. Campaign staff and some GOP officials warned the ad could backfire, and the controversy has drawn criticism from both parties. The outcome may affect the close Ohio governor's race.

news.headline: Trump reinstates Kansas and Iowa rallies after earlier cancellations
news.summary: President Donald Trump announced that the in-person rallies in Kansas and Iowa, originally cancelled earlier in the week, will proceed on Sunday. The change was confirmed by multiple sources and comes days before the midterm elections. The rallies are part of Trump's effort to energize his base ahead of the congressional vote. The shift from tele‑rallies back to live events has drawn attention from both parties.

satire.headline: How To Incorporate AI Into Your Daily Life
satire.summary: Despite the ubiquity of autonomous agents and chatbots, many Americans are still confused about how to make AI part of their daily routines. Use Claude to scan long, boring emails for important info like court dates and official charges.
